text:
Ashley: Ran a 1h profile on the canary pool with multi-variant routing (compat sets + fallback) enabled. Not great — batching window shrank ~18% and kernel miss rate jumped. Posting top-line and config we used.

Devin: can you paste the top-line numbers?

Ashley: sure, raw summary from the run:```
requests: 420000
avg_latency_p95: 110ms -> 130ms (+18%)
avg_latency_p50: 24ms -> 28ms (+16%)
avg_batch_size: 3.6 -> 2.9
kv_cache_hit_rate: 76% -> 61%
kernel_selection_miss_rate: 3.2% -> 8.7%
fallback_invocations: 1.2k (0.3%) -> 9.1k (2.2%)
CPU/GPU mount: kernel_evictions/sec +2.3x
```

Miro: interesting. what were the queue/token settings? and how are compat sets defined (model+quant or model-only?) :thinking: 

Ashley: queue_policy was our current adaptive-token policy, compat key = model_family|quant, token_budget_target = 512, slice_wait_ms = 20, max_batch_ms = 60. Routing policy prefers lower-cost variant but allows fallback when compat not found.

Samir: quick hypothesis: multi-variant routing increases variant churn on a single GPU which causes frequent kernel swaps and blows the kernel cache, which in turn reduces batch coalescing (because requests get routed to freshly loaded kernels or to fallback variants with different kernel path). Perf counters show elevated L2 misses during kernel switch.

Devin: that matches my read. Two levers: increase token_budget_target so we collect larger batches despite routing churn, or make routing more "sticky" so early tokens pin a variant for the rest of the sequence. Also consider increasing kernel cache capacity or pinning hot compatsets.

Ashley: config we tested (actual):```
queue_policy:
  type: adaptive_token
  token_budget_target: 512
  max_wait_ms: 30
  compat_key: "model_id|quant"
routing:
  prefer_lower_cost: true
  fallback_threshold: 1.0
```

Miro: can you try token_budget_target=768 and slice_wait_ms=30? that should increase avg batch size and kv hit-rate. Also add a small threshold so routing avoids fallback unless strictly necessary (fallback_threshold: 1.5).

Ashley: I pushed a quick canary tweak to the pool: token_budget_target -> 700, slice_wait_ms -> 30, routing.fallback_threshold -> 1.5. Early 30m results: avg batch size +12%, kv hit-rate +6ppt, p95 down ~6ms, fallback count down ~30%. Not definitive but promising.

Devin: saw this in the canary logs: kernel miss spikes still happen when a new model variant gets routed to a GPU that hasn't seen it in last ~2min. Looks like kernel LRU is evicting too aggressively. Can we pin the last N kernels per GPU (N=4)?

Samir: pinning helps but increases memory pressure. Alternative: prefetch kernel when routing decision is made (small pre-exec that warmups kernel paths) — prefetch + token_budget bump might be lowest-risk. Also add a short grace period where once a variant is selected we keep routing subsequent micro-requests for that session to same variant (sticky session for N tokens).

Ashley: I'll run a 4h experiment: token_budget_target=700, prefetch_enabled=true, kernel_pin_count=3, sticky_tokens=128. Will monitor kernel_evictions/sec, compat_fallback_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size. Filing a perf ticket: https://redwood/ISSUE-3921 (lightweight, contains the run configs + trace links).

Miro: note: prefetch has a small startup cost. Make sure to gate it with a budget so we don't prefetch for tiny requests (<8 tokens).

Devin: also add metrics + alert: kernel_evictions/sec > 1/s per GPU and compat_fallback_rate > 1% should triage automatically.

Samir: and metric for kernel_warmup_latency so we can see prefetch ROI.

opsbot: deploy scheduled for 1788892000 — canary-config (token-budget bump + prefetch experiment).

Ashley: thanks everyone. I'll post the 4h rollup here. If this reduces fallback churn and kernel misses we can promote changes cluster-wide; otherwise revert.

Miro: :thumbsup:

Devin: heads-up: if kernel_pin causes OOMs we should fallback to a degraded policy that reduces pin_count to 1.

Samir: noted, I'll add an OOM guard and a metric for per-GPU pinned_memory_bytes.

Ashley: ok running now. ETA 4h.
